title: A person types chrome://crash/ in a page's address bar: the renderer ends, the app stays, the tab shows the sad tab and Cmd-R brings the page back
preconditions: private scratch config (driver_app: bench config, ui.animations.enabled false)
a fresh saved session: one workspace, one terminal tab
the loopback web fixture (webfixture.py) serves tests/oracle/fixtures/web as $WEB
Chromium is the default browser engine (browser.defaultEngine unset)

allow_crashes.reason: crash-renderer opens chrome://crash/ on purpose: the debug URL ends that page's renderer

steps.note: a script run files the Chromium tab at the end of the pane and marks it agent-driven. Only `before`: until its page reports a title, the tab's title is its URL, which holds the fixture's port
Select Tab 9 shows the last tab, the page, so Chromium makes its browser; the wait is for its finished load, which comes after its title
the shown page has the keyboard, so Cmd-W closes it
Cmd-W closes the page into the closed history; closing it ends its agent marks (TabContentCache.release)

Shift-Cmd-T reopens the page from its record as a person's tab, so a debug URL typed in it takes Chromium's debug-URL path and never meets the agent URL guard (CEFAgentURLGuard). The input turn only: show-reopened takes the settled checkpoint once its load finished
Select Tab 9 shows the reopened page; the wait is for its finished load
the address bar of the reopened page takes the keyboard (Chrome's FocusLocationBar); no browser.page call, so the tab stays a person's
the facets outside the browser before the child exit; after-child-exit must equal them

expect.noReceiptReason: typing in the address bar runs no registry action; Return opens the typed URL as the person's

steps.note: a person types chrome://crash/ (Shift-; is the colon; with the trailing slash, the URL Chromium compares, the address bar completes no chrome page) and presses Return: the debug URL never commits and ends the page's renderer (third_party/blink/public/common/chrome_debug_urls.h kChromeUICrashURL). The only page tab, so no other tab shares that renderer. Only `before`: crashed-tab takes the settled checkpoint once the tab shows the crash
the crashed tab is an error state (the sad tab, Chrome's crashed_status), not a closed tab
equal to before-child-exit: a Chromium child exit changes no workspace, pane, window, terminal, notification or setting
the retry: Cmd-R (browserReload) loads the page again in a new renderer; crashed turns false when that load starts (BrowserTabStateMachine .started), so retry-loaded takes the settled checkpoint
the retry loads the page the tab showed: the debug URL never committed

invariants: the app pid does not change (driver_app fails the case when it does): a Chromium child exit never ends the app (content/public/test/browser_test_utils.h CrashTab)
after-child-exit equals before-child-exit: no workspace, pane, window, terminal, notification or setting changes with the child exit
no step calls a crash method of the app: each exit comes from a Chromium debug URL or a kill of the child, so Release gets no new crash entry point
crash-renderer raises crashes.counts.renderer by exactly one and no other kind (I17: allow_crashes renderer, max 1)
the crashed tab shows an error state with retry (tabs crashed true), and Cmd-R brings it back (crashed false, loadState finished, the same url)
teardown: quit the tagged app the run started and its tag's daemons (TagTeardown)
verify its debug socket is gone
untested: pointer entrypoints (no pointer op in case-v1): the sad tab's Reload button
the page's own content and pixels after the exit: no facet reads a page's DOM or its frames
chrome://crash/ in an agent-driven tab (the agent URL guard refuses it; the guard's own case)
chrome://kill/ (the same path as chrome://crash/ with another exit reason)
